rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Judgment Day, deniers from each community will be classified by the nature and extent of their sins and sent to their allotted part of Hell, as 15:44 describes.
rows.anchor: the basis of the nature and extent of sins committed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fawj denotes the large multitude of deniers; their number cannot trouble God or exhaust Hell, which will swallow whole armies and ask for more.
rows.anchor: The word ﻓَﻮۡج refers to the large number of those who denied.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rejecting resurrection and retribution for lack of exhaustive knowledge is invalid: signs in intellect, nature, and the world suffice, and only the Creator knows every cosmic secret.
rows.anchor: To acknowledge something, it is enough that signs and proofs exist in its favour in human intellect and in human nature

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demand for exhaustive knowledge is foolish, like denying the Himalayas because one has not seen every peak and valley.
rows.anchor: one who denies the existence of the Himalayas because he has not seen all its peaks and valleys.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waqa'a al-qawl means God's decision to consign wrongdoers to Hell; they cannot answer the preceding question, and the verdict is carried out.
rows.anchor: the verdict here refers to God’s decision of consigning all

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that they cannot speak should be read with 36:65, where God seals their mouths and their hands and feet testify.
rows.anchor: should be understood in the light of the following verse of Sūrah Y āsīn

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By linguistic parallelism, a word equivalent to maẓliman is omitted from the first clause and another from the second, exemplifying a concise style discussed elsewhere.
rows.anchor: In accordance with linguistic principles, parallel words are suppressed in this verse.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb yu’minūn expresses intention; only those intending belief see the signs, while the obdurate have no intention to believe.
rows.anchor: only those people can see them who intend to believe.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse censures people demanding a punishment sign: night and day display God's power and wisdom, but only those intending to believe perceive the signs.
rows.anchor: This verse censures those who were demanding the sign of punishment

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an's signs summarize proofs of the Creator's power, wisdom, providence, monotheism, and the Hereafter; the context especially points to resurrection, mirrored in daily sleep and waking.
rows.anchor: rather succinctly refers to all of them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night-to-day cycle is a daily reminder of resurrection, and the supplication before sleep recalls this reality.
rows.anchor: The supplication before going to sleep at night also reminds people of this reality.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trumpet's blast will terrify creation; only those God wills will be safe, and verse 89 elaborates this concise description.
rows.anchor: Only they will be secured from the upheaval of that day who the Almighty will intend.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People of every rank, leaders and followers alike, will appear before God in humiliation; only those already excepted will be safe.
rows.anchor: People of high and low status as the leaders and their followers – everyone will appear before God in humiliation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains' flight like clouds evokes the Day's horror; classical Arab sages and poets considered everything besides mountains mortal.
rows.anchor: everything except the mountains to be mortal.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction ṣun'a Allah, like wa'da Allah and ṣibghata Allah, directs attention to God's work: the One who made everything firm will expose the mountains' fragility.
rows.anchor: This style is adopted when it is specifically meant

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final clause explains why the horrors are described: God knows all their misdeeds and will therefore bring them to justice.
rows.anchor: when He is aware of them, He will definitely bring them to justice.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The just verdict for the righteous and wrongdoers follows necessarily from the previous verse's account of God's knowledge of their deeds.
rows.anchor: God’s verdict will be pronounced with justice for the righteous and the wrongdoers.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the sūra's close, God states the Prophet's mission decisively, giving Quraysh the chance to mend their ways or face the consequences.
rows.anchor: Here, at the end, God has explained through the tongue of the Prophet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the author's view, context implies a suppressed 'say' before 'I have only been commanded,' as later commands to say confirm.
rows.anchor: because of concomitant indications: this is evident later

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse refers to Makkah and the House's history: the Prophet was chosen to revive the purpose for which God made this land sacred, and will not be diverted.
rows.anchor: The verse refers to the land of Makkah and history of the House of God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As the centre of Abraham's religion, Makkah's true mission is to call people to one God; the Prophet rejects its pagan worship and is commanded to worship and obey God alone.
rows.anchor: the real task that should be carried out here

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet has no duty to satisfy Quraysh's demands: he must recite the Qur'an and warn them, while its benefit depends on their response.
rows.anchor: He has been directed to read out the Qur’ ān to them. Its benefit or lack of it will depend on the attitude they adopt.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham had asked God to send an Ishmaelite messenger to recite the Qur'an and purify people through law and wisdom; the Prophet fulfills that same mission, which listeners must join or face its consequences.
rows.anchor: whose task would be to read out the Qur’ ān to them and purify them through law and wisdom (62:2).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to thank God for revealing the Qur'an; if people disregard it and demand punishment signs, God will soon show them those signs.
rows.anchor: The Prophet (sws) is asked to tell them that only worthy of

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fata'rifūnahā means they will realize they were warned by the person they rejected and called to bring their doom, but that realization will not help them.
rows.anchor: at that time will these people realize that they had been warned of someone who they rejected and called for their doom.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final clause warns that God knows their pranks and will hold them accountable, though every task has its appointed time.
rows.anchor: not remain under the misconception that God is unaware of their pranks.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These words bring the sūra's explanation to its culmination, prompting gratitude to God.
rows.anchor: With these words, the explanation of this sūrah reaches its culmination with the grace and help of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God destroys a city only after its people wrong themselves by persisting in polytheism and rejecting a messenger despite warnings; Quraysh now face the final stage, and any punishment after respite is their own injustice.
rows.anchor: God did not destroy a city unless its inhabitants become unjust to their own selves.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing Quraysh's leaders directly, the author contrasts their brief worldly luxury with God's better, lasting reward for those who seek the Hereafter, urging them not to squander it.
rows.anchor: The previous warnings were indirect. This verse directly addresses the leaders of the Quraysh.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muḥḍarūn evokes people brought as bound criminals: those promised an everlasting kingdom will receive it, while those given transient pleasures will be dragged shamefully before God; the former fate is better.
rows.anchor: The word إﺣﻀﺎر means to bring someone tied up as a criminal

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coming passage refutes polytheism and the belief that alleged partners or intercessors could benefit their worshippers in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: a refutation of polytheism and idols

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alleged partners have no role in administering the world and cannot help their worshippers in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: have any role in administering this world

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who reject the Qur'an on the basis of these baseless entities should reflect carefully on their fate.
rows.anchor: Those who were denying the message of the Qur’ ān on the basis of
